title: china limits fuel price increases third time since iran war began 2026 09 11
text:
BEIJING, Sept 11 (Reuters) - China has capped increases in retail prices ​for transportation fuels for the ‌third time since the Iran war began to mitigate the impact ​of rising international oil ​prices on the domestic market, the ⁠state planner said in ​a statement on Friday.
Retail prices for ​gasoline and diesel will rise by 260 yuan ($38.76) and 250 yuan per ​metric ton, respectively, effective September ​12. Under China’s scheduled pricing mechanism, the ‌increases ⁠would have been 435 yuan and 420 yuan, respectively, the statement said.
After the adjustment, gasoline ​and ​diesel retail ⁠prices will be 19% and 21% higher, respectively, ​than the levels set ​in ⁠the last adjustment before the Iran war began.
($1 = 6.7087 Chinese ⁠yuan ​renminbi)
